text:
marie: quick sync — i'm putting up a short design for a "phased demonstrator" traffic guardian. goal: let staged/A-B variants get traffic while giving an automated, very fast evacuation path that minimizes user-visible failures. want thoughts on state boundaries and safety levers.

devon: pinged — high level diagram? where lives the decisioning?

marie: controller (control-plane) owns policy, probe configs, and long-lived trial metadata. runtime adapters (edge proxy + instance agents) make the fast-path decisions. key primitive = a lightweight "traffic-guardian token ledger" and a soft lease per session.

ashley: soft lease? how does that work for long-lived chat sessions or streaming responses?

marie: lease = ephemeral sticky mapping: session_id -> variant_token with TTL (default 10m). runtime checks token validity before routing. on critical failure we either revoke the token or emit an override that forces route to baseline within a tight window. streaming: we flush partial responses to baseline model only if probe signals allow safe continuation.

devon: what constitutes a "critical failure"? latency spikes? quality regression?

marie: composition of signals. typical policy sample: error_rate > 1.5% OR p99_latency_delta > 200ms OR model_quality_score drop > X. we keep thresholds conservative and require hysteresis.

tj: can you paste a compact policy proto?

marie: sure — pseudo: ```text
guard_policy {
  probe_interval: 5s
  error_rate_threshold: 0.015
  p99_latency_delta_ms: 200
  quality_regression_score: 0.08
  min_samples: 200
  action_on_violation: { primary: immediate_reroute, secondary: throttle_trials }
}
```

ashley: how do we avoid a big thundering fallback where baseline can't handle load?

marie: two mitigations: 1) capacity-aware gradual reclaim: runtime asks controller for reclaim_budget and rate_limit. 2) degraded evacuation path — route to a "reduced-TPS" variant (quantized or cached) as interim. controller holds emergency capacity tokens per-region.

devon: storage for ledger — centralized DB = latency risk. local caches + CRDT-style lease?

marie: exactly. prefer hybrid: compact global offsets (consensus-backed, low QPS) + local ephemeral leases in each proxy. Protocol: controller writes trial-state (allowed_percent, emergency_tokens) to consensus; proxies reconcile and make per-request decisions. reconciliation window = ~1s.

rollout-bot: draft RFC uploaded: https://redwood.internal/rfc/phased-demonstrator-guard-v1 (auto) :eyes:

ashley: KV-cache warming and prefix states — if we flip routes, warmed KV caches will be cold on baseline. any playbook?

marie: two approaches: speculative warmup during pilot (mirror small fraction of requests to baseline for warmup), and a short-lived optimistic read-through cache that seeds baseline with recent KV. both need strict privacy guards (no PII mirroring).

devon: what about the operator surface? how do SREs perform manual override?

marie: operator API: snapshot current trial, force_reclaim(percent|all), dry-run simulation that emits expected latency/cost delta for reclaim. also a safe-mode that pauses automatic reclamation for a trial for 30m.

tj: failure modes: split-brain between proxies and controller under network partitions?

marie: runtime-first safety: local proxies favor conservative choices if controller unreachable (i.e., prefer baseline). controller consensus cluster is HA, but proxy local decisioning prevents single-point stalls. we log a partition metric and surface to oncall.

devon: observability — what do we emit?

marie: every request tags: trial_id, allocation_path (sticky|reclaimed|mirrored), decision_reason (probe|operator|policy), latency_ms, token_revoked boolean. rollups: per-tenant SLO violations, reclaim_events, capacity_token_utilization.

ashley: sounds solid. question: is this tied to our existing rollout API or a new controller?

marie: integrates with rollout API but uses a separate "guardian" microservice that subscribes to rollout events. we keep the rollback semantics in rollout API but let guardian manage in-flight reclaim and fast-path actions.

devon: perf target for cutover?

marie: per-rpc switch target <= 200ms for path-change decisions; full traffic reclaim should be tunable but default aim = 5s for large reclaims (protect baseline).

rollout-bot: note: i'll create a follow-up issues list based on this thread.

ashley: ok — leaving a few inline comments in the RFC. sgtm in principle. :+1:

tj: sgtm — let's run a small canary with mirror-warmup and measure reclaim delta.

marie: thanks all — i'll fold comments into v1 and schedule a cross-team sync next wed.
